headline: Alcaraz vs Shelton: the US Open quarter that New York wanted
whyCareReason: A defending champion back from a four-month wrist layoff against a home lefty on Ashe. No 2026 champion yet.
teaser: Quarter-final, 8-9 September. Alcaraz beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4. Shelton beat Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4. They meet next.
story:
Why this one matters: the US Open is still live. Do not write a champion. Write the match that sits in front of you.

Carlos Alcaraz is the defending champion, back from a right-wrist injury that kept him out about four months. He opened against Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 and then beat Tommy Paul 6-4, 6-3, 6-4. Ben Shelton, the eighth seed, beat Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 and called Alcaraz's return superhuman. Fireworks on Tuesday night, he said.

If Alcaraz wins he likely sees Tiafoe or Michelsen in a semi. The American men have not had a Slam champion since Andy Roddick here in 2003. That is the air in the building. The match is the thing.
stakes: A quarter-final that can send a favourite into an American semi, or send New York into orbit.
